style._claimMarkerComment: The trailing marker a CLAIM-BEARING bullet must carry (gate C25). Pack data: the gate holds no marker literal. It is also the first entry of bulletTrailingAllowed, so C17's trailing-punctuation rule already tolerates it.

rules.description: Legacy title ≤200 chars (in force until Jul 27 2026 cutover)
Title ≤75 chars effective Jul 27 2026 (all categories except media); violators subject to AI auto-rewrite (14-day review window for Brand Registry owners)
Item Highlights ≤125 chars, searchable, effective Jul 27 2026; absorbs title overflow; may not be writable in all templates yet (seller-reported error 100476)
No word appears more than 2× in the title (brand counts; short prepositions/articles exempt)
Banned title characters: ! $ ? _ { } ^ ¬ ¦ ; avoid en dash (normalize to hyphen/comma)
Exactly 5 bullets for 3P sellers, ≤255 chars each
Description ≤2000 chars, plain text with blank-line paragraphs
Backend search terms: ≤249 UTF-8 BYTES saved (US); exceeding de-indexes the entire field; no brands/ASINs/disease terms; no title repeats
Main image: pure white RGB 255/255/255, product ≥85% of frame, longest side ≥1000px; regulated panels (Supplement Facts) must be real photographs
Premium A+: up to 7 modules, 1464px wide; Basic: 5 modules, 970px

Style/formatting: sentence case (no ALL-CAPS words ≥4 chars outside the acronym allowlist), bullets start with a capital and carry no trailing punctuation (a trailing '*' claim marker or ')' is allowed), no ™/®/©/€/emoji, no ASINs in copy, no promotional terms in title surfaces
No price/$ in A+/images; no unsubstantiated superlatives; no star/review claims; no urgency; no guarantees; no Buy Now / Subscribe & Save in A+

prohibitedContent._comment: Amazon bans price/availability/condition details and contact info in titles, bullets, descriptions, backend and images (A+ included). Patterns are pack data; the gate reads them.

prohibitedMarketing._comment: Amazon-prohibited MARKETING claims: urgency, guarantees, rank/best-seller, star ratings, review counts and false regulatory-approval claims. PACK DATA — gate A8 (A+ surfaces) and C19 (every surface) read these patterns; the gate holds no literal marketing lexicon. C19 additionally scans compliancePack.superlativeBans. GUARANTEE PATTERNS target the CLAIM, not the word: "money back guarantee", "satisfaction guaranteed", "guaranteed results", "results guaranteed", "lifetime guarantee" and the first-person promise "we/our guarantee" all fail, while the bare noun in a non-promissory sentence (an image brief that says "no guarantees or claims on pack") does not. A bare \bguarantee[ds]?\b flagged every sense of the word and was a live false positive on ordinary copy. Note "we cannot guarantee ..." is deliberately NOT matched: only a positive first-person promise is a guarantee claim.
patterns: clinical-endorsement claim (borderline: legitimate when substantiated, banned here because Amazon treats unsubstantiated clinical framing as a prohibited claim)

units._comment: Unit lexicon for the gate (C10/C12/A5) and the deterministic facts producer. PACK DATA — lib/gate and lib/engine hold no unit literals. Order inside each list is irrelevant; the gate compiles longest-first alternations.
units._familiesComment: Units that are the SAME physical dimension and must be compared with each other (first entry is the canonical family name).
units._daySupplyCuesComment: A day figure is only measured against facts.daySupply when one of these cues sits next to it. Without them, stock copy like 'Give it 90 days' was failing C12 as a contradicted supply claim.

factFields._comment: Snapshot attribute keys read by lib/engine/facts.ts. PACK DATA so the facts producer holds no category attribute-key literals.

titleWordRepetition._comment: Gate C1 sub-rule: no stemmed content word may appear more than `max` times in the title.

aplusModuleCues._comment: Substring cues gate A4 uses to locate the required A+ modules by id.

_about: OPERATOR CHECKLIST — the publish-time procedure the ship sheet renders.
It is DOCUMENTATION, not enforcement: nothing here can fail a check, so it is
deliberately NOT a REQUIRED_PACK_PIECES row (emptying it disarms nothing).
It lives here so lib/export holds no marketplace procedure of its own.
publishOrder:
Description — paste as ONE line; the
tags render the paragraphs
Backend search terms (Keywords tab, Search Terms field)
Attributes — every blank costs a customer-facing search filter
A+ content from the module copy below
Subscribe & Save enrolment — enrol the SKU in Manage Subscribe & Save once the offer is live and in stock
Recommended browse node LAST — set it only after everything above is saved
operatorChecklist.propagationNote: Allow up to 48 hours for saved changes to propagate to the live detail page. Do NOT re-submit the same edit while it is propagating: duplicate submissions queue behind one another and a stale one can overwrite a newer value.
operatorChecklist.browseNodeNote: The recommended browse node is a SUGGESTION only — confirm the node is accepted in the Product Classifier before saving, and enter it LAST.
operatorChecklist._opsPlaceholdersNote: WS7 SUPERSEDED this list. It held two hand-written reminders (a TIC/cGMP line and a rating line) that named the topic without stating the rule, the date it takes effect, or what happens if it is missed. Both are now structured rows in postPublish.marketplaceChecklist, which the sheet renders with lane, effective date and volatility. The key stays (empty) so an operator pack can still add its OWN account-specific placeholders without touching the marketplace checklist.

_attributeGuardComment: AM-1 / C24 — the DOSAGE-ATTRIBUTE guard, ported from the harness kit's checkC24. Structured attributes are FILTER-FED: a strength figure sitting in an attribute whose KEY names a dose states that number AS a dose, which overstates the product even when the number itself is the canonical one. `keyPattern` is matched against the attribute KEY (case-insensitive); `unitDimensions` names which `units.dimensions` lists supply the hero units the VALUE may not assert beside a number. The figure belongs in copy attached to the blend or formula, never in structured data. Emptying either field disarms C24, so both are REQUIRED_PACK_PIECES.
_outputHygieneComment: C27 — OUTPUT HYGIENE. Three properties of machine-written copy no other check looks at: (1) generated copy must be pure ASCII, which it is by construction because the ENGINE folds typographic punctuation at emit (lib/engine/typography.ts) — anything left is a real character a human must decide about; (2) it carries none of the model's stock phrases; (3) it never echoes a fragment of its own instructions (a live run once shipped an image brief quoting the compliance instruction back at us). Every list is pack data and every one of them is a REQUIRED_PACK_PIECE, because emptying one disarms that third of the check.

outputHygiene._asciiExemptSurfacesComment: FALSE-POSITIVE REDUCER for the ASCII rule only (emptying it makes the gate STRICTER, so it is deliberately not a REQUIRED_PACK_PIECE). Backend search terms are the one surface where non-ASCII is the POINT: the field exists for other-language variants and misspellings, and stripping the diacritics off a Spanish or German keyword removes the query it was added to match. The phrase scans (AI tells, leaked instructions) still cover it, and every customer-facing surface stays ASCII-only.

_bulletArchitectureComment: WS4 — BULLET ARCHITECTURE (pack data). The five bullet SLOT JOBS from the playbook's copy phase (B1 hero spec + named entities; B2 primary benefit cluster; B3 heritage/completeness + secondary use-case; B4 certifications + allergen + safety; B5 routine/usage/storage). Rendered into the bullets prompt so every bullet is written to a DECLARED job with its own situational anchor, and read by the AUDIT lint (lib/audit/diff.ts) which reports an unfilled job or a repeated anchor as a P2 gap. STRATEGY IS NEVER A GATE: nothing here can fail a run — the gate holds hard rules only.

slots.job: Primary benefit + primary keyword, carried by the hero spec and the named entities
slots.guidance: Open on the headline benefit in the primary keyword's own words; state the hero figure attached to the blend or formula (never to a serving) and name the entities by their full label names.

slots.job: Mechanism / differentiator — what makes this formula work the way it does
slots.guidance: Name the mechanism or the structural differentiator (delivery form, stability, pairing, sourcing) and tie it to the benefit as cause and effect, not as an adjective.

slots.job: Secondary use-case — the second situation this product is bought for
slots.guidance: Take the second-largest query family (travel, evening routine, post-workout, a second audience) and answer it in one self-contained, quotable sentence fragment.

slots.job: Quality / trust — certifications, testing, manufacturing and the allergen declaration
slots.guidance: State the verifiable trust facts (testing, certifications, manufacturing standard, origin) and close the bullet with the allergen declaration as its final, trailing clause.

slots.job: Audience fit + routine — who it is for, how it is used and how it is stored
slots.guidance: Say who the product is for in their own words, then how it fits a day: dose timing, what it is taken with, and storage.

bulletArchitecture.anchorRule: Each bullet carries ONE situational anchor — a concrete moment, audience or environment — and no two bullets may share one. An anchor is the sentence a retrieval engine can quote back to a shopper who described that exact situation.

allergenPosition.rule: When a bullet declares an allergen, the declaration is a TRAILING clause in the bullet's final segment - never its opening words and never its colon header. The bullet must earn its read on the benefit first; a declaration placed first turns the whole slot into a warning label.

_positioningAnchorComment: R48 — POSITIONING ANCHOR (pack data). Playbook 8.20: do not compete on a spec you cannot defend. A per-serving arms race against a rival's number invites both a compliance mismatch and a losing comparison; panel-verifiable completeness and heritage are defensible because a competitor cannot copy them by reformulating. Injected into the copy prompts and rendered as a STRATEGY NOTE in the ship-sheet header. Advisory guidance — no check reads it.

positioningAnchor.headline: Position on completeness, not on a spec race.
guidance: Anchor the value story on what the label can verify in full — breadth of the formula, the completeness of the panel, heritage and process — rather than on a single headline number.
Never frame a figure as out-scoring, doubling or overtaking a rival's number: a figure a competitor can overtake by reformulating is not a position.
When a number is used, attach it to the formula or the blend it is actually measured over, and let the completeness story carry the premium.
positioningAnchor.sheetNote: Strategy (R48): this listing is positioned on panel-verifiable completeness, not on a spec race. If you edit the copy, keep the value story on breadth and process — a headline number a competitor can leapfrog by reformulating is not a defensible position.

_keywordRulesComment: WS3 — the KEYWORD SYSTEM (playbook Phase 7 + gate C28).
PACK DATA: every surface name, status word and threshold the placement check reads
lives here, so lib/gate holds no keyword vocabulary of its own.
The model is QUALITATIVE — the playbook forbids search-volume tools and this system
calls none: a term earns its tier from evidence, never from a number an API returned.

demandRecapture.headline: K4 — DEMAND RECAPTURE: never abandon the demand behind a term you may not write. Map it to a compliant cluster and record the route.
mappings: Named-condition demand maps onto the compliant structure/function cluster the category already uses (balance, flora, pH, everyday comfort language). Write the cluster; record the banned term as captured-via with the cluster named in via.
Condition-intent demand maps onto the INGREDIENT NAMES themselves — for that intent the ingredient is the search term. Name every entity in full and let the ingredient carry the intent.

Symptom-word demand stays in customer review language, which is where buyers are allowed to write it. Your copy mirrors only the compliant half of the pair (the everyday, qualified phrasing) and never the symptom word itself.

Every candidate term passes a four-test screen before it may be placed: legality, marketplace policy, substantiation, and conversion economics. A term can be lawful and still be strategically negative when the intent it brings converts badly.

keywordRules.sheetNote: Every PLACED term below was machine-verified to appear on each surface it declares; every BACKEND-only term was verified to sit in the search-terms field and nowhere a customer can read; every NEGATIVE term was verified to appear nowhere at all. Rival brand names belong in the negative list — they are a trademark exposure, not an opportunity.

_postPublishComment: WS6/WS7 — the POST-PUBLISH phase the ship sheet renders.
GUIDANCE TIER, exactly like operatorChecklist: the app SURFACES these, it does not DO them,
and nothing here can fail a check — so it is deliberately not a REQUIRED_PACK_PIECES row.
It lives in the pack so lib/export holds no marketplace procedure and a rule change is a data edit.

operatorPanel._comment: WS5.5 - the operator panel-confirmation step. The wording lives here because it names a category artifact and lib/engine may hold no category vocabulary (tests/category.literals.test.ts).
operatorPanel.promptHeadline: OPERATOR-CONFIRMED SUPPLEMENT FACTS PANEL (PRODUCT TRUTH for this run). The operator read these values off the physical label and confirmed them, so they OUTRANK anything scraped from the live listing and outrank the CANONICAL FACTS above wherever the two disagree. Write them exactly as given: never round them, never re-derive them, never improve on them, and never state a panel value the operator did not confirm.
operatorPanel.inputHelp: Paste or type the values you read off the physical label, one per line as key: value (for example serving_size: 1 Capsule). Confirmed values become product truth for this run: the copy is written from them and the gate checks every surface against them. Nothing here is saved to the knowledge pack.

qaPolicy.headline: Answers only.
notes: Answering customer questions from the seller account is fine; creating questions about your own product is not. Use these as prepared ANSWERS when a real customer asks.
The pack ships prepared ANSWERS to be used when real customers ask, spread over the first two weeks - never self-posted questions.
Posting the questions from your own account violates Amazon Community Guidelines and puts the ASIN's entire review history at risk.

timingAdvisory.headline: Timing: do not judge this change for two to four weeks, and time events six to eight weeks out.
notes: Reindex and semantic-layer propagation are slow. Allow 2-4 weeks of steady data before judging whether a change worked, and never revert after three days: an early dip is the index re-settling, not a verdict.
Time any event, promotion or traffic push 6-8 weeks AHEAD of when you need it to land, so the reindex and the assistant-model incorporation have both happened by then.
Field edits themselves propagate to the live detail page within about 48 hours. Do not re-submit the same edit while it is propagating.

Re-run the assistant interrogation monthly: ask it what the product is for, whether it is third-party tested, how it compares, and whether it is good value. Every wrong or missing answer is the next fix.

postPublish.marketplaceChecklistNote: These are ACCOUNT-SIDE actions. This app cannot perform any of them and has checked none of them - it surfaces them so they are not discovered late. Every row marked ⚠ carries a date or a list that moves: re-verify it live before you rely on it, including the version printed here.

marketplaceChecklist.title: File the cGMP certificate and current COA through an approved TIC provider - the same day you publish.
marketplaceChecklist.detail: Third-party cGMP verification submitted through a marketplace-approved Testing/Inspection/Certification provider is mandatory for every dietary supplement listing on the US marketplace, across all supplement categories, with roughly a 90-day window. Non-compliance means suppression or removal, so this is listing survival, not paperwork. HOLDING the documents is not compliance - they must be FILED (Seller Central > Manage Your Compliance > Select a Provider). First-party audits and regulator inspection history are not accepted; some existing certification programmes fast-track. The approved-provider list is refreshed MONTHLY: take it live at filing time and never trust a cached copy, including any list quoted in your own internal documents.

marketplaceChecklist.title: Treat a 4.0-star rating as a discovery floor, and run rating defence from day one.
marketplaceChecklist.detail: Measured assistant recommendation samples contain essentially nothing below 4.0 stars, so the rating behaves as an AI de-selection gate rather than a soft signal - and in-stock plus fast fulfilment are near-prerequisites alongside it. Stand up the rating-defence routine before the first order: daily review monitoring, prepared compliant response templates, and the Brand Registry review-contact workflow. Never incentivise a review. If the listing sits just above the floor, defence is existential rather than cosmetic.

marketplaceChecklist.title: Hold external traffic until week 7 or later, and stage it behind rating gates.
marketplaceChecklist.detail: Publish and stabilise first: conversion assets have to be proven before you pay to send strangers at them. Sequence owned email, then the marketplace creator/affiliate programmes, then attribution-tracked affiliate platforms, then performance-PR placements, with small bridged paid tests last. Gate scaling on rating (a 4.2-star scaling floor and mandatory bridge pages until 4.3 is the pattern that worked). BANNED, all of them manipulation-policy violations: search-find-buy schemes, super URLs, and rebate programmes. Every off-marketplace asset goes through a compliance screen FIRST - off-site copy about a regulated product is still regulated speech.

marketplaceChecklist.title: Vine is for a child ASIN under 30 reviews - an established ASIN is ineligible.
marketplaceChecklist.detail: Enrolment is limited to variation/child ASINs below the 30-review threshold, with per-parent fee tiers. Check eligibility before it appears in a launch plan: an established ASIN with a large review history cannot use it, and planning around a tactic the account cannot run costs a launch window.

marketplaceChecklist.title: Allow 48 hours for a saved edit to propagate. Do not re-submit it.
marketplaceChecklist.detail: Description and field edits take up to 48 hours to reach the live detail page. Duplicate submissions queue behind one another and a stale one can overwrite a newer value, so re-submitting the same edit while it is propagating is how a correct value gets replaced by an old one. Verify rendering after propagation, not during it. Editing a listing can also trigger the marketplace AI enhancement pass - copy that already matches the canonical shape gives it nothing to rewrite.

marketplaceChecklist.title: Re-verify every dated rule monthly - including the ones printed in this sheet.
marketplaceChecklist.detail: Marketplace listing policy changed twice in a single half-year during the source project. Monthly: re-run the assistant interrogation diagnostic, re-check the approved TIC provider list (it is refreshed monthly and providers drop off it), and confirm the browse node and product-type token have not drifted. Any cached list is a liability the moment it is written down, this document included.

_imageArchitectureComment: WS8 — the VISUAL PRODUCTION architecture (playbook Phase 11).
PROMPTS ONLY: this project writes briefs, the operator renders them and controls the spend.
requiredTokens are what gate C29 verifies the EMITTED brief actually says. Each group is one
requirement written in every spelling we accept; ALL groups on a slot must be satisfied.
Two images may NEVER be AI-generated or AI-altered whatever else changes: the main bottle

Two images may NEVER be AI-generated or AI-altered whatever else changes: the main product photograph and the printed label panel. Where the category is regulated the panel is a compliance document and the parity
anchor the enforcement AI compares the copy against, which is why its slot carries the
real-photograph requirement as a machine-checked token group rather than as advice.

slots.guidance: The real bottle photograph on a pure white background. State the background as pure white RGB 255/255/255, the product filling at least 85% of the frame, and a longest side of at least 1000px. Say plainly that it is a real photograph of the actual bottle and never AI-generated. No badges, no overlay text, no borders.

requiredTokens.label: product fills at least 85% of the frame

slots.guidance: Benefit infographic carrying the headline spec, phrased as the label attaches it. Legible overlay text at phone size: if a phone camera app can copy the text off the image, the assistant can read it too.
What is inside and how much of it: the format, the count, and the daily routine. Overlay text states figures only as the label states them.
Every named component written out in full, with substantiated certification marks as legible badges. Name the entities: they are what an assistant lifts when a shopper asks what is in it.
Lifestyle frame shot in the environment the buyer is actually in when the need arises, not a generic studio scene.

A real photograph of the printed information panel on the physical label - the facts panel, ingredient list and warnings where the category has them, otherwise the printed back label. Sharp, evenly lit, fully readable, every row visible. Never AI-generated and never AI-altered: where the category is regulated this image is a compliance document and the anchor the marketplace scan compares the copy against.

requiredTokens.label: a photograph of the printed panel or label
a real photograph, never AI-generated or altered

slots.guidance: Own-line comparison or problem-to-solution frame. Compare against a generic unnamed alternative only: naming a rival brand is a trademark exposure.
The routine: when to take it, with what, and how it fits a day. Storage note if the format needs one.

guidance: Problem to solution, in that order, with the product on screen inside the first three seconds.

Every on-screen string is customer-facing copy and is scanned exactly like a bullet: no cost figures, no rating or review marks, no promise about outcomes or returns, no urgency wording, and no named condition.
Assume it is watched muted: the on-screen text has to carry the whole message on its own.
Shoot for the vertical frame from the start rather than cropping a wide edit down to it.

aplusNotes.brandStoryCard: The Brand Story module is a separate carousel that renders across every ASIN in the brand, ABOVE the product A+ module. It carries its own card set, its own background image and its own headline; the copy below is the product A+ and does not populate it. Build the Brand Story once at brand level and it appears on every listing you own.
aplusNotes.bannerAlt: Every A+ banner image carries its own ALT text, capped at the same 100 characters as a gallery image. It is invisible on the page, which is exactly why a stale agency template naming a rival brand survives there for years. Set it on day one and check the live values.
aplusNotes.carouselTrim: A+ image carousels are trimmed on render: a card set built at full length will not all display, and the cards past the cut are not indexed either. Front-load the cards that matter and treat the tail as expendable rather than assuming all of them show.
aplusNotes.premiumScope: Premium A+ (the wider layout, in-module video and hover/hotspot cards) is deliberately OUT OF SCOPE for this app: it changes the module set and the asset specs, and generating copy against a tier the account may not hold would produce a pack that cannot be pasted. The modules below are the standard tier.

_bulletFormatComment: WS10 / R4+R6 — the two BULLET FORMAT rules that are deterministically checkable (gate C31).
R6 COLON HEADER. The marketplace documents the bullet pattern as a header fragment, a colon,
then the body ("Cotton fabric: Made from 100% cotton"). A bullet with no header is a sentence
in a list, and it also loses the scannable label a mobile reader actually reads.
R4 WORD REPETITION, and why the cap is 3 rather than 2. The TITLE rule is at most twice and C1
enforces exactly that. A BULLET is different: it names the dosage form, the count and the routine
in one sentence, so "One capsule daily: 60 vegetable capsules ... at one capsule per day" uses the
same content word three times and is ordinary, correct copy. Setting the cap at 2 would fail it,
and failing lawful copy trains an operator to ignore the gate. A FOURTH occurrence is not that
shape any more - it is stuffing, which lowers the assistant trust score. So the cap is the
stuffing floor, not a style preference. Raise it in pack data if a category genuinely needs to.
Title Case per word and the write-out-numbers-under-ten rule are deliberately NOT here: both have
legitimate exceptions this system cannot distinguish (registered ingredient marks keep their own
casing; measurements stay numeric), so they stay prompt-guided, exactly as the playbook left them.
_copySurfaceNotesComment: WS10 — two facts about HOW the marketplace renders these fields that decide whether the copy works,
and that neither the gate nor the generator can enforce because they are about the reader, not the text.
Rendered beside the field they are about, so they are read where they are acted on.

copySurfaceNotes.descriptionWithAplus: R12: keep this field FILLED even once A+ is live. A+ body text is not indexed by classic search - the description is, and the shopping assistant reads it directly. Moving indexable copy out of the description and into A+ loses the indexing and keeps none of it.
copySurfaceNotes.mobileFrontLoad: R11: on mobile the description renders ABOVE the bullets and is truncated behind Read more, and chat takes half the screen. Whatever has to be read has to be in the first two lines - the rest is opened by a minority.
copySurfaceNotes.brandConfirm: CONFIRM - scraped value. This came off the live page, not from the Brand Registry, and a scraped brand string is routinely a seller-entered variant. Check it against Brand Registry before it goes anywhere near a feed: it is backend-only and must never appear in customer copy.
